nodes.label: About Icon
nodes.description: Circular teal/cyan icon with a stylized italic lowercase letter 'i', representing the universal 'information' or 'about' symbol. Used as the UI icon for the application's About dialog/section in the E-Tipitaka PC application.

nodes.label: Information / About Action
nodes.description: The 'about' or 'information' UI concept — invoking it typically opens an About dialog showing application metadata (version, credits, license, contact).

nodes.label: Books Icon (Stack of Three Purple Books)
nodes.description: Stylized icon depicting a stack of three purple/magenta books with white pages, used as a UI element to represent books, library, scriptures, or reading material in the E-Tipitaka application. Likely represents access to the Tipitaka volumes/scripture collection.
nodes.norm_label: books icon (stack of three purple books)

nodes.label: Library / Scripture Collection Concept
nodes.rationale: A stacked-books visual is a conventional UI metaphor for 'library' or 'collection of texts'. In the context of E-Tipitaka (a Buddhist scripture reader), this icon most plausibly signifies access to the Tipitaka book collection or volume browser.

nodes.label: Clear Icon (Broom/Sweep)
nodes.description: A small icon depicting a yellow broom/whisk-broom with a wooden handle and purple band, sweeping a small dust particle. Represents the 'clear' action — used in UI to clear input fields, search results, history, or selections.
nodes.ui_purpose: Button or icon to clear/reset content (e.g., clear search box, clear selection, clear results)

nodes.label: Clear Action
nodes.rationale: The broom metaphor is a common UI convention to convey 'sweeping away' content — clearing inputs, resetting state, or removing items. Chosen over a trash/delete icon because clearing is non-destructive (resets a view) rather than permanently destroying data.

nodes.label: Close Icon (Red X Button)
nodes.description: A glossy red circular button with a white 'X' shape in the center, used as a UI icon to represent a close, dismiss, cancel, or remove action. Typical use cases include closing a tab, dialog, panel, or removing an item from a list.

nodes.label: Close/Dismiss Action
nodes.rationale: Represents the user-facing action of closing, cancelling, or removing an element. Red color signals destructive/exit semantics; X shape is a universal close affordance.

nodes.label: Font Size Down Icon
nodes.description: Toolbar/UI icon depicting a capital letter 'T' next to a downward-pointing arrow. Represents the action of decreasing the displayed font size in the E-Tipitaka reader interface.

nodes.label: Decrease Font Size Action
nodes.rationale: Provides users with accessibility/readability control to shrink Tipitaka text rendering. Pairs with a complementary 'font size up' control for symmetric zoom-style typography adjustment.

nodes.label: Import Icon
nodes.rationale: Small UI icon depicting a globe/world overlaid with an orange/yellow upward-pointing arrow. Represents an import action — bringing data from an external source (web/world) into the application. Used in the E-Tipitaka PC application to denote import functionality, likely importing bookmarks, notes, or data from external sources or other E-Tipitaka installations.

nodes.label: Import Action
nodes.rationale: The conceptual action of bringing external data into the E-Tipitaka application, visually represented by an upward arrow over a globe.

nodes.label: Enter Key Icon
nodes.description: Icon depicting the Enter/Return key, showing a downward-then-leftward arrow inside a key outline. Represents the action of submitting input, confirming a search, or executing a command in the E-Tipitaka UI.

nodes.label: Submit/Confirm Action
nodes.rationale: The Enter key icon visually communicates to users that pressing Enter triggers submission, typically used to execute a search query in E-Tipitaka's search interface.

nodes.label: Keyboard Shortcut Hint
nodes.rationale: Used as a UI hint or tooltip indicator to inform users which keyboard key activates a function, improving discoverability of keyboard shortcuts.

nodes.label: Mark 5 Color Marker (Pink/Coral)
nodes.description: A small solid pink/coral colored swatch image used as a visual marker/highlight indicator in the E-Tipitaka PC application. Part of a numbered series of color markers (mark1-markN) likely used to color-code bookmarks, highlights, or annotations in Tipitaka text passages.

nodes.label: Color-Coded Bookmark/Highlight System
nodes.rationale: Numbered mark icons (mark1, mark2, ... mark5, ...) provide users with multiple distinct colors to categorize bookmarks or highlights in scripture text. Pink/coral as the 5th marker offers visual differentiation from earlier markers in the sequence.

attributes.description: A small circular dot/ring glyph representing the Pali/Sanskrit niggahita (anusvara) diacritic mark, used in Thai-script Pali transliteration. Renders as a tiny open circle (วงกลมเล็ก) typically placed above a consonant to indicate a nasal sound.
attributes.purpose: UI icon resource for inserting or representing the niggahita diacritic in the E-Tipitaka search/reader interface, likely used to support Pali text input or display in the Thai Tipitaka reading application.
attributes.domain: Pali script / Thai Buddhist scripture rendering
attributes.rationale: E-Tipitaka deals with Pali Tipitaka texts; the niggahita ('นิคหิต' / ํ) is a special character not always easy to type, so a dedicated icon/button asset facilitates input or visual marking in the UI.

nodes.label: OK / Confirmation Checkmark Icon
nodes.description: A circular green glossy button with a white checkmark, typically used as an OK/confirm/success indicator in a UI dialog or button.
nodes.visual_style: green circle, glossy/3D button look, white check (tick) mark

nodes.label: Confirm / Accept Action
nodes.rationale: Green checkmark icons are a near-universal UI metaphor for confirming or accepting an action; the icon communicates a positive/success outcome to the user without requiring text labels.

nodes.label: Right Arrow Icon
nodes.description: A circular green icon with a white right-pointing arrow inside. Represents navigation forward, next page, or proceed action in the E-Tipitaka PC application UI.

nodes.label: Navigate Forward / Next
nodes.rationale: A right-pointing arrow universally represents forward navigation, next item, or proceed actions. The green color suggests an active/enabled state.

nodes.label: Search Icon (Magnifying Glass)
nodes.description: A magnifying glass icon used in the E-Tipitaka UI to represent the search action. Visually, a circular lens with a diagonal handle. Represents the search/find functionality in the application.

nodes.label: Search Action
nodes.rationale: The magnifying glass is a universal UI metaphor for search. Used in the E-Tipitaka application to allow users to query Tipitaka scriptures.

nodes.label: Thai Language Mode (Tho Than - Royal Thai Script)
nodes.norm_label: thai language mode (tho than - royal thai script)

nodes.label: White Background Image
nodes.description: A small solid white PNG image used as a background or placeholder asset in the E-Tipitaka-PC application UI. Likely used for blank states, spacers, default backgrounds, or as a base layer for compositing other UI elements.

nodes.label: UI Background Asset
nodes.rationale: A plain white image serves as a neutral background or placeholder in the UI, providing a clean canvas for text rendering and visual layering in the Tipitaka reader interface.
